title: Enterprise invoice adjustments and refund playbook
text:
Enterprise invoice adjustments and refund playbook

description:
Problem statement: As Redwood expands enterprise contracts and runs pricing/packaging experiments, we see increasing manual work from billing ops for invoice-level adjustments: post-issue credits, negotiated discounts, multi-month proration for reserved capacity, refunds for trial overages, and contract-level offsetting credits. These manual adjustments are slow, error-prone, and cause poor enterprise experiences and delayed revenue recognition. Scope: define an operational playbook, decision matrix, and self-service flows for common invoice/metering edge cases (credits, overages, refunds, proration, negative balances) plus triggers from enterprise security questionnaire answers that affect billing data retention/export. Out of scope: replacing core billing engine; this is a policy + small product surface work + ops automation to reduce triage time.

acceptance_criteria:
A documented decision matrix for at least 8 common invoice adjustment scenarios (post-issue credit, negotiated invoice-level discount, reserved capacity prorate, partial-month cancellation, trial overage refund, negative balance carry-forward, billing reconciliation after plan change, emergency goodwill credit)
Self-service portal flow defined for small credits (< $1,000) that allows CS/SEs to issue credits with audit trail; UI/console mocks linked and signed off by Design
Automation tickets created for two low-effort ops automations: (1) automated pro-rate calculator for reserved capacity cancellations, (2) emit structured adjustment events to downstream ledger for audit and reporting
SLA for billing ops triage time reduced from 48h to 8h for standard cases (procedural + templates in playbook)
Security questionnaire guidance (data retention, export formats, encryption of billing exports) drafted and reviewed by Security and Legal
End-to-end test plan and example invoices for each scenario committed to the billing repo (links in comments)

comments:
2025-02-11: Kickoff with GTM, Legal, Security, and Billing Ops. Consensus: prioritize reducing manual triage for post-issue credits and reserved capacity proration. Outcome: 8-scenario matrix and two automation proofs of concept (POC).
2025-02-14: PM sync - decided to treat negotiated contract concessions differently: require an "approved concession" tag and Legal sign-off. Action: create a lightweight concession approval form (Confluence: /billing/contract_concessions).
2025-02-18: Design review - provided initial mockups for self-service credit issuance in Console. Design feedback: show original invoice line items, auto-calc pro-rate, and require a short justification for audit. Design owner: Priya Nair (link: https://drive.google.com/designs/billing-credit-ui).
2025-02-21: Engineering grooming - ENG-2910 will add "adjustment_event" to ledger API; ENG-3174 will implement pro-rate calculator service. Trade-off discussed: align to existing invoice schema vs new adjustment records. Decision: add adjustment records to preserve original invoices immutable. (GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/402).
2025-02-24: Security questionnaire input: Security asked for retention options (30/90/365 days) for raw per-token usage payloads. Recommendation: default 90 days for hosted customers, and expose export hooks for enterprise with contract-specified retention. Legal requested template language for SQS export and KMS encryption. (Doc: https://confluence.redwood/invoice-billing/retention-guidance).
2025-02-27: Billing Ops pilot: ran 12 historical adjustment requests through draft playbook. Time to resolution median 10h (vs 48h baseline). Noted two missing cases around partial refunds during multi-month reserved commitments — updated matrix and created follow-up tasks.
2025-03-02: PM review with finance - need explicit GL mapping rules for credits vs refunds to avoid revenue misclassification. Finance asked for a cutoff policy: credits < $500 treated as billing ops adjustments, >= $500 escalated to Finance review. Added to acceptance criteria.
Next steps: finalize playbook doc, ship Design mocks, create two engineering tickets for POC, and schedule Legal + Security approval for the concession flow.
